title: Blest Are the Pure in Heart
description: Blest Are the Pure in Heart in Tonic Solfa to FRANCONIA: the solfa with the words, staff notation, the four verses, and a piano.
about: John Keble wrote the first and third verses, dated 10 October 1819, as part of a longer poem published in The Christian Year in 1827; the second and fourth come from the Mitre Hymn Book (1836), edited by William John Hall. The tune FRANCONIA was published by Johann Balthasar König in 1738.
underlay: Blest are the pure in heart, For they shall see our God; The se-cret of the Lord is theirs; Their soul is Christ’s a-bode.

lines: Blest are the pure in heart,
For they shall see our God;
The secret of the Lord is theirs;
The Lord, who left the heavens
Our life and peace to bring,
To dwell in lowliness with men
And for His cradle and His throne
Give us a pure and lowly heart,
